name: gpt56sol-page-4-library-recovery
paragraphs: the North Harbor Public Library recovery team are preparing to reopen the second floor on tuesday, September 15, after a water pipe burst above the local history room. Facilities manager Priya Nair said the leak were discovered at 6:40 a.m., but the overnight alarm never send a notice because two sensors was configered to the wrong zone. By the time a custodian arrived, water had spread under 14 shelving units and several seperate archive boxes was becoming soft around there edges. The team moved 326 books, 48 photograph folders, and seven framed maps into the Cedar Conference Room, where portable fans has been running since Friday. Nobody are allowed to return an item to public shelves until conservator Daniel Ortiz checks it for moisture, mold, and loose binding glue. The first inventory list were wrote quickly and it contain duplicate call numbers, missing author names and dates that dont match the catolog. Priya asked every worker to initial each line after they verify it, however some volunteers was signing before the item had actually been inspected which make the record unreliable. The library definately needs a clearer sequence because staff currently walks between rooms with no consistent route, they often handle the same box twice while another box sits unrecorded.

during monday's planning meeting Daniel explain that damp paper should dry slowly, yet one employee had pointed a heater directly toward a nineteenth-century atlas and nearly warped its pages. He told the group to use fans for air movement and blotting paper for wet covers, direct heat is prohibited. The revised workflow have four stations: intake, condition review, drying, and final catalog check. At intake, one person records the item number and another person photographs the damage; at condition review, Daniel decides if the item can remain onsite or must go to Lakeside Conservation Lab. Each stations need a blue tray for pending items and a green tray for completed items, but the supply order only included three blue trays and two green one. Operations coordinator Malik Brooks promised to borrow the missing trays before 8:30 a.m. on September 14. The software used for tracking recovery items also behaves inconsistantly: it sometimes saves a blank location, it changes semicolons into commas and the search page don't show records created after noon unless users restart it. Technicians has reproduced the issue on Windows 11 and Ubuntu 24.04, however they haven't determine whether a compatability problem, the database index or the browser cache cause it. Until that problem is fixed, workers must export a local CSV every two hours and store it on drive RECOVERY-02, no one may email the file or upload it to a cloud service.

the reopening plan says the second floor will opens at 10:00 a.m. on September 15, but only if the humidity stays below 55 percent for twelve continuous hours and Daniel approves the final inspection. Visitors will be able to use study tables and the computer lab, the local history room remains closed through September 22. Signs at both stairwells should explain the closure in English and Spanish, although the current spanish translation uses a word that means temporary sale instead of temporary closure. Malik will ask translator Elena Vega to correct the notice by September 13 and Priya will print 20 copies after Elena confirms the wording. Staff also needs to contact 63 patrons whose reserved books was moved during the emergency; the message should state where pickup occurs, how long the hold remains active, and who to call if an item appears damaged. The draft message is too vague and sounds blaming, it says patrons should of checked the website even though the website was unavailible for six hours. Before doors open the team must test elevator access, emergency lighting, public computers, catalog search, and the fire alarm connection. A supervisor will record each result on form NHPL-R2-0915 and unresolved failures is reported to Priya immediatly. If any safety test fails, or if humidity rises above the limit, reopening are delayed without exception. The team wants the public update to be calm and useful but it also need to be honest about damaged materials, restricted areas, and the work that remains.
